1

Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P.No.559 of 2014, the appellants / claimants have come before this Court challenging the same by filing the present civil miscellaneous appeal.
2. The claimants are the wife and children of the deceased Kittu @ Krishnan.

On 31.05.2014, the deceased was driving a two wheeler bearing Registration No.TN-21-AQ-3282 near Mahendra city,
G.S.T road and when he was nearing the turn, he accidentally fell from the two wheeler and sustained severe injuries.
He was admitted in the SRM Hospital on the same day and died on 06.06.2014.
The claim petition was filed claiming a compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- for the death of the deceased Kittu @ Krishnan.
The first respondent is the owner of the vehicle and the second respondent is the insurer of the vehicle.
3. Before the Tribunal, a counter affidavit was filed by the second _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent /
Insurance Company denying the allegations made in the claim petition that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the rider of the motorcycle.
It was also alleged that as per the Accident Register, the deceased was admitted in the Hospital by his friend Vijay and the doctor has recorded "Alleged h/o RTA self driven two wheeler".

Further, in the Accident Register of the SRM Hospital, it was recorded by the doctor as "alleged h/o RTA while riding a two wheeler and accidentally fall from it and sustained injuries on 31.05.2014 at about 4.30 p.m. near Mahendra city".
The Insurance Company also denied the allegations made in the FIR that one Anand has driven the vehicle and that the said Anand has no valid driving licence on the date of the accident.
The Insurance Company also reiterated that if really one Anand had driven the motorcycle, he would admitted the deceased in the Hospital.
However, the deceased was admitted in the Hospital by a person named Vijay.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation as claimed in the claim petition.
4. Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants, P.W.1 to P.W.3 _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis were examined and Exs.P1 to P7 were marked.
On the side of the respondents, R.W.1 was examined and Ex.R1 to R5 were marked.

The Tribunal, on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that though the accident occurred on 31.05.2014, FIR was lodged only on 06.06.2014 wherein it was stated one Anand had driven the vehicle and given the fact that one Vijay had only admitted the deceased in the Hospital and the name of Anand was nowhere stated in the Accident Register.
The said Anand as alleged in the FIR was no way responsible for the accident.
The Tribunal also took into consideration the delay in lodging the FIR on 06.02.2014 at 06.00 p.m.

Moreover, the Tribunal heavily relied upon the endorsement made in the Accident Register of the SRM Hospital stating that "Alleged h/o RTA while riding a Two Wheeler and accidentally fall from it and sustained injuries on 31/05/2014 at about 4.30 pm near Mahindra city"

Relying upon the said fact and the materials placed on record especially Ex.P1-FIR and Ex.P7-charge sheet, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the deceased was responsible for the accident due to rash and negligent _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis driving

and therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation, holding so, the Tribunal dismissed the claim Muthulakshmi vs S.Parthiban on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161943609/
2 petition.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the second respondent / Insurance Company.
6. This Court carefully considered the submissions made on either side and the materials available on record.
7. It is true that the accident occurred on 31.05.2014 and FIR was lodged on 06.06.2014 and that there was a delay in lodging FIR.

Though it was alleged that one Anand has driven the vehicle and the deceased was a pillion rider, there was no eye witness to the accident and a person by name Vijay has only admitted the deceased in the Hospital.
Even in the Accident Register, it was stated that, there was alleged fall from the two wheeler and the deceased was self inflicted.

That apart, this Court has already held in C.M.A.No.2805 of 2019 dated 05.05.2022 by relying the judgments in the _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis case of V.Thanikachalam v.
C.Premlatha and another reported in 2003 AIHC 3864 and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., v. G.P.Chandrasekar and another reported in 2012 (1) TN MAC 548 that the person, who has made the entry in the Accident Register has to be examined in order to prove the veracity of the same.

sentences.text: Unless this procedure is adopted, the entry in the Accident Register cannot be looked into.
8. In the judgment second cited, this Court has observed that the informant as per the Accident Register would have given information without knowing the exact facts.
Therefore, the subsequent Police investigation and the charge-sheeting should not be looked suspiciously unless it is proved that the investigation was not fair and impartial.

9. In the instant case, there was no eye witness as to the manner in which the accident took place, the number of persons who travelled in the two wheeler and the person who was responsible for the accident.

That apart, the doctor who made the e n d o r s e m e n t a s " s e l f d r i v e n " i n t h e A c c i d e n t _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Register of the Hospital, has not been examined.
But that alone cannot be put against the claimants.

Since unless it is proved contrary,
the investigation is presumed to be fair and impartial.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal was incorrect in coming to the conclusion based on the delay in lodging FIR and non-examining of the informant.
Considering all the above materials, this Court is of the opinion that finding of the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition is erroneous, the same is liable to be set aside and is hereby set aside.
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled for compensation.
10. As far as quantum of compensation is concerned, it is the claim of the appellants that at the time of accident, the deceased was a Carpenter and also earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

The appellants failed to file any material with regard to Muthulakshmi vs S.Parthiban on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161943609/
3
income earned by the deceased.
Hence, this Court is inclined to fix a sum of Rs.6,000/- as monthly income of the deceased.
11. As per Ex.P2 / Death Certificate, the age of the deceased is 42.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2009 (2) TNMAC 1 SC [Sarla Verma & Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & another]

sentences.text: , the multiplier applicable is '14'.
There are three dependants of the deceased and 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Thus, a sum of Rs.6,72,000/- (Rs.4,000/- X 12 X 14 ) is awarded towards loss of dependency.

In addition to the above, it would be just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards loss of consortium to the first appellant / wife of the deceased, Rs.40,000/-
each towards loss of love and affection to the appellants 2 & 3, who are the daughters of the deceased, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation to hospital, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
12.

In the above circumstances, this Court is inclined to fix the compensation under the below mentioned heads :-
 S.No Head of Amount awarded  Compensation by this Court

1 Loss of dependency Rs.6,72,000/-
 _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  S.No Head of Amount awarded  Compensation by this Court

2 Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
 3 Loss of love and Rs.80,000/-
 affection  4 Transportation to Rs.10,000/-
 hospital  5 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 6 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 Total Rs.8,32,000/-
13.
In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed.
A sum of Rs.8,32,000/- is awarded as compensation to the appellants with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The first appellant being wife of the deceased is entitled to a sum of Rs.3,32,800/- (40%) and the appellants 2 and 3, who are the daughters of the deceased, are entitled to Rs.2,49,600/- (30%) each as Muthulakshmi vs S.Parthiban on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161943609/
4 compensation.
The appellants are directed to pay necessary Court fee, if any on the compensation awarded by this Court.

The second respondent / Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, within a period of four weeks from the _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the first appellant is permitted to withdraw her share now determined by this Court, along with proportionate interest and costs.
Though the second appellant at the time of filing the claim petition was a minor, now she would have attained the age of majority, hence the second appellant is also permitted to withdraw her share.
The compensation payable to the minor third appellant is directed to be deposited in a Nationalised Bank in an interest bearing account.
Till such time the minor attains majority, the mother or legal guardian, as the case may be, shall withdraw the interest alone once in three months for the welfare of the minor.

Upon attaining majority and upon proper proof being filed substantiating attainment of majority, the Tribunal is directed to transfer the share of the third claimant directly to her Bank account through RTGS.
No costs.
